attribution_invariant: A failure may be classified as provider or transport only when a dispatch attempt is proven and provider/transport evidence supports that classification. Absence of provider evidence is never evidence of provider failure.

events.event: Gemini seat produced no move at the second elenchus and at reconstruction
events.original_attribution: Gemini seat failed with no response body; framed as provider unreliability and used to justify migrating google-vertex/global/flex -> google-vertex/global
events.remaining_uncertainty: None on classification. The exact refused request bytes were never persisted, so a byte-for-byte replay is impossible; only the body digest survives.
events.supporting_evidence: Terminal accounting recorded both attempts: 14 turn records against 12 consumed calls, worst_case_picodollars 0, transport_completed false. The two calls google-vertex/global did dispatch both returned HTTP 200.

events.event: Gemini seat returned an invalid structured Socratic follow-up at the second elenchus
events.original_attribution: Q2c stopped because output envelopes did not separate reasoning from visible answer; Gemini was grouped with GPT-5 Mini under that shared local-envelope cause
events.remaining_uncertainty: The retained evidence establishes a provider structured-output contract violation; it does not identify whether the upstream model or provider enforcement layer produced the invalid payload.
events.supporting_evidence: Dispatch completed with HTTP 200 and finish_reason stop. The provider returned content as an empty object despite the strict wire schema requiring seven fields; local validation rejected all seven as missing. The response used 761 completion tokens, including 739 reasoning tokens, but did not exhaust the 4,096-token envelope.
